name: TCEQ "Sanitary Sewer Overflows (SSO)" dataset on data.texas.gov (8kc5-95uk)
operator: Texas Commission on Environmental Quality, Office of Compliance and Enforcement
waters_covered: statewide; receiving_water_body free text (often "NO WATER BODY PROVIDED" / "Not Provided"), river_segment code
access_detail: Socrata SODA: https://data.texas.gov/resource/8kc5-95uk.json ($where, $order, $limit; no key needed for light use). 56,545 rows on 2026-11-03; start dates 2010-09-02 to 2026-08-29; latest received 2026-08-31; rows last updated 2026-09-24 (dataset created 2025-07-17; metadata says "Update Frequency: Semiannually"). 2016-2025 about 3,800 to 6,000 a year; 2026 to August 3,185. About 33,330 rows name a water body. Samples raw/tceq-sso-sample.json, raw/tceq-sso-recent.json, metadata raw/tceq-sso-meta.json.

sample_record.source: Pump line at Lift Station No. 4
sample_record.incident_description: (trimmed) bypass pump line broke; untreated sewage to ground and a storm drain; about 39,000 gallons

cadence: Refreshed in batches (last 2026-09-24, holding reports received to 2026-08-31): one to four months behind. Reports to TCEQ are due within 24 hours (5 working days written).
license: No licence stated in the dataset metadata (licenseId null); data.texas.gov site terms apply.
status_reason: Statewide, daily precision, stable incident number, volume, cause, permit and often a named water body, 16 years. No coordinates (county and address text only) and a lag of months.
notes: Geocode from incident_description addresses or the regulated entity (RN) location; river_segment gives the TCEQ classified segment when not 0. incident_description, incident_action and incident_comment are free text written by reporters and may name contractors or people: run the name blocklist before display.

name: TCEQ "Reporting Unauthorized Discharges and Sanitary Sewer Overflows" guidance page
access_detail: Fetched. 24-hour notice to the regional office; written report in five working days; monthly summary (TCEQ-20756) allowed for small qualifying spills; public/media notice criteria from 30 TAC 319.302; confirmation to TCEQ within 48 hours of public notice.

name: 30 TAC 319.302 Notification Requirements and 319.303 Notice to Local Officials and Local Media
access_detail: Read via LII (the SOS TAC viewer has moved). Notice to local government officials and local media for (1) any spill likely to affect a drinking-water source, (2) 50,000 gallons or more near a drinking-water source or in a sensitive area (recharge zone, karst), (3) 100,000 gallons or more; within 24 hours; hand delivery, fax, email or phone with written follow-up; copy to the TCEQ regional office within 48 hours. 319.303 sets content and precautionary statements ("avoid contact with spill material, soil, or water in the affected area").
status_reason: The public-notice duty: media and local officials only, above 100,000 gallons (or 50,000 near water supplies).

name: Texas General Land Office Texas Beach Watch (BW2025_Summary MapServer)
waters_covered: 174 stations at about 61 Gulf beaches (Aransas, Brazoria, Cameron, Galveston, Harris, Jefferson, Kleberg, Matagorda, Nueces, San Patricio counties)
access_detail: https://gisweb.glo.texas.gov/arcgis/rest/services/BW/BW2025_Summary/MapServer/0/query?where=1%3D1&outFields=*&f=json (public). 174 rows on 2026-11-03; Advisory values "Low" and "Medium" seen (the site maps these to advisory recommended or not; high = advisory); cfu, Measurement ("5 MPN/100ml"), Date of last sample, plus 2023-2025 summary statistics per station (samples, geomean, advisories, percent days under advisory). Behind www.texasbeachwatch.com (ArcGIS JS 3.45; email alert sign-up alertSignup.cfm). Sample raw/tbw-sample.json.
cadence: Weekly March to October, every two weeks otherwise; advisory resampled every 24 hours. Layer updated as results are entered.
history: current state plus 2023-2025 summaries; the service name changes yearly (BW2025_Summary)
status_reason: Machine-readable coastal advisory feed; local governments post signs; Galveston County Health District issues the Galveston advisories.
notes: Watch for the service name changing (BW2026_...).

name: City of Houston Public Works monthly SSO reports and maps (consent decree Paragraph 61)
operator: City of Houston, Houston Public Works
waters_covered: Houston bayous (Buffalo, Brays, Sims, White Oak, Greens, Halls)
access_detail: Monthly SSO summary report PDF plus an SSO map PDF, filed under the 2021 wastewater consent decree (U.S. and Texas v. City of Houston, 4:18-cv-03368, S.D. Tex.). Table: SSO ID, TPDES permit, address, reached waters (Y/N), estimated gallons, structure, cause, start and end times, corrective action. Late 2022 to at least August 2025 seen in search; not fetched.
status_reason: Adds start/end times for Houston; the TCEQ dataset already carries the events.

name: EPA SOBE (eRule) extract, Texas rows
access_detail: 8 Texas events from 5 permits (TX0032735, TX0053074, TX0081264, TX0117501, TX0140848), latest start 2026-04-01. Texas permittees report to TCEQ, not NeT-SewerOverflow. raw/sobe-tx-rows.json.
status_reason: Too sparse; TCEQ dataset is the feed.

name: Texas 89th Legislature (2025) bills on overflow notice
access_detail: No 2025 bill on public notice of sewage spills found. SB 565 (2025, enacted per Plural Policy) amends Water Code 7.0026 on water and sewer entities (text not read). 2015 HB 2051 / SB 912 (1,000-gallon threshold, monthly reporting for small spills) and 2013 HB 824 preceded the monthly-summary rule.
status_reason: No change to the public duty found.
